title: Responding to negative Google reviews
context: Small businesses freeze on 1-star reviews. The question is what to say, how fast, and whether to reply publicly or go private first.

title: Getting more customer reviews without being pushy
context: Owners assume asking is annoying. The right moment, channel, and script lifts response rates 3-5x without losing the room.

title: Why star rating alone doesn't predict customer trust
context: 4.9 with 12 reviews beats 4.4 with 400 for raw rating but loses on trust signals. Recency, response rate, and photo count matter more than owners think.

title: The hidden cost of unanswered reviews
context: An unanswered review is a dropped conversation in public. Google's local pack appears to weight response rate; conversion funnels prove it.

title: Multi-location review management without going insane
context: 10+ locations, each with a manager who thinks review response is HQ's job. The SLA, the template library, and the escalation path that actually scale.

title: Using reviews as a lead magnet
context: Asking in person vs. SMS vs. post-purchase email — each has a different conversion rate and a different kind of review at the end of it.

title: Response templates for one-star 'didn't read the menu' complaints
context: The customer is wrong on the facts, publicly. A template that defends the business without looking defensive, in under 60 words.

title: When to publicly rebut a dishonest review vs. let it sit
context: Public rebuttal can backfire — the Streisand effect is real. The rule of thumb for which fights are worth having and which die faster unanswered.

title: Why a 4.7-star business can lose to a 4.3-star one
context: Review recency, response rate, and photo count move the local-pack ranking even when average rating is lower. Fix the three inputs you control.

title: Chain franchises: enforcing review-response SLAs across 20+ locations
context: Without a 9-5 ops manager, you need a system: shared template library, response-time SLA, per-location scorecard, and a Friday escalation ping.
